pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/toast/Toast.tsx:22 The region is always mounted, but its text is written straight into it with no node keyed to each announcement, so the same receipt shown twice in a row (e.g. a retried act that fails the same way) makes no DOM change and is not spoken the second time; a correct shell scheduler still could not force a remount through this primitive.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/toast/Toast.tsx:22 The region is mounted before any news (role=status at :21), which is good. But there is no keyed remount or clear-then-set, so a repeat is a no-op. The shell's scheduler (app/(studio)/_shell/toast.ts showToast) also replaces the open receipt rather than queueing it, so in a burst only the last write is heard.

packages/ui/src/components/field/Field.module.css:5 Field, Select and Search remove the app-wide 2px focus outline (this unlayered module beats @layer base) and replace it with a 1px border at .55 alpha, a weaker indicator than the one removed. app/globals.css says to tint the border as well as the outline, not instead of it. The focus-ring probe only walks app/ and components/, so it never checks packages/ui.

packages/ui/src/components/toggle/Toggle.tsx:34 The free-form `name` replaces the visible label instead of starting with it. Call sites set label "live" with name "arm live, now dry", and label X with name "mechanism X", so the spoken name differs from the drawn word (label-in-name) and the live one also writes state into the name next to aria-pressed. Field.tsx:26 (required aria-label) and Button's required `label` are conformant.

packages/ui/src/components/fold/Fold.tsx:56 Fold renders its body only after the first open, then hides it with the `hidden` attribute, which closes the visual and accessibility channels together from one condition. When closed, the Toast holds no text and does not mount its ledger link.

packages/ui/src/components/button/Button.tsx:63 Native button, a/select/input everywhere; label required; aria-pressed on Toggle and Seg; disabled is honest (it stays in the tab order). Caveat: a disabled `submit` Button still submits its form when activated, because aria-disabled does not block native submission, so every form's onSubmit has to re-check busy itself (HuntShelf.tsx:38, ScheduleForm.tsx:103).

packages/ui/test/components/controls.test.ts:130 The primitive tests regex-match SSR markup for attributes (role, aria-pressed, aria-live) instead of querying computed names by role or the sequence of announcements. Nothing announces the same text twice, so the repeat-silence defect passes. This is the attribute-as-proxy trap the gate-sees-target law names.
